title: The Linen Contract That Fits on Paper
summary: Arithmetic and finance check: all displayed calculations reconcile using the supplied 3.8x factor. Hospital finishing intensity is 0.5×0.5 + 0.5×1.1 = 0.8 hours per thousand pounds. Baseline peak load is 2.0M×60%/1,000×0.8 = 960 hours, a 160-hour shortfall; this displaces 160/0.4×1,000 = 400,000 lb and $0.24M contribution. No-build annual cash flow is $1.20M − $0.15M − $0.24M = $0.81M and NPV is $0.81M×3.8 − $0.20M = $2.878M ($2.88M). Build cash flow is $1.20M − $0.15M − $0.25M = $0.80M and NPV is $0.80M×3.8 − $1.20M − $0.20M = $1.64M, hence a −$1.238M baseline build disadvantage. At 75%, peak load is 1,200 hours, shortfall 400 hours, displaced incumbent volume 1.0M lb, displacement cost $0.60M, no-build cash flow $0.45M, and no-build NPV $1.51M. The stated $0.13M build advantage is correct. The crossover is also correct: required avoided displacement is $0.25M + $1.20M/3.8 = about $0.5658M annually, implying about 0.943M lb displaced, 377.2 shortfall hours, 1,177.2 total hospital finishing hours, and 1,177.2/1,600 = 73.57% (about 73.6%); the 75% schedule is about 1.43 percentage points above it. The case otherwise meets the requested 7-section/4-exhibit/23-calculation shape, has integrated-exhibit reasoning, a hand-manageable chained calculation, valid like-for-like NPV comparisons, and a coherent conditional recommendation—subject to the missing machine-capacity fact and the telegraphed pivot above.

issues.where: q4 share / q6 calculations and recommendation
issues.problem: The machine’s peak-finishing capacity is never quantified. The q4 share says it “can process all of the hospital’s peak finishing load,” when the known load is only the 960-hour baseline; q6 then assumes build NPV remains $1.64M at the 1,200-hour revised load and recommends a commitment to any peak share above 73.6%. Those conclusions require the machine to cover at least the additional 400 hours at 75%, and the open-ended “above 73.6%” recommendation also requires an upper capacity limit. No such capacity input is available. Thus the pivotal build comparison and robustness recommendation are not verifiable from candidate-visible facts.
issues.fix: State a machine capacity explicitly before q6—for example, “the machine adds 800 aggregate peak finishing hours, so total spare finishing capacity becomes 1,600 hours and it can support the full 2.0M-lb hospital contract even if 100% falls in peak weeks.” This makes the unchanged $1.64M build NPV and the crossover recommendation runnable. Alternatively, state its actual maximum and limit the schedule condition to the feasible range.

issues.where: Clarifying delivery-schedule answer; q2 model answer, hints, and pushback; difficulty design
issues.problem: The required curveball is substantially telegraphed rather than functioning as a pivot. Before any analysis, the clarification explicitly says the hospital “may change its delivery schedule,” and q2 then directs attention to cadence/schedule changes and says the investment depends on peak share/crossover. A candidate is therefore primed to expect exactly the q5 reveal, undermining the specified mid-case new-information curveball and reducing the intended test of revising a conclusion under pressure.
issues.fix: Remove the advance statement that the hospital may change its schedule. Keep the baseline schedule as the current contractual proposal, and deliver the 75% concentration only after the baseline recommendation. In q2, allow cadence to arise as one possible candidate idea, but remove the explicit schedule-change/crossover framing from the model answer, hint, and pushback.
